He makes a point of showing you that you can use it for non-steam games. They just have to be added to steam and run through big picture.

Only if you want to remap the keys. By default, you've got the stick and dpad mapped to the arrow keys, A,X,B, and Y mapped to Space, R, E, and F respectively, left and right triggers mapped to right and left click respectively (Yes, they're reversed, makes sense when you use it), left grip mapped to Mouse3, right grip mapped to Control, and the two bumpers mapped to scroll up and down. Start is mapped to Escape, and the back button is mapped to Tab.

For a lot of games it'll work without configuration, otherwise you can change the controls in the game itself if the game allows you to.

I've used it in non-Steam games with no issues, except one VR game that mapped left and right arrow keys to turn instead of strafe and didn't let me change them. I've even used it to watch netflix from the couch, A mapped to space lets you pause easily, and you can go forward or back with the stick or dpad easily.

You'd only have to use Steam if you want to remap the keys (for example the gyro is great for FPS games but isn't enabled on desktop) or use the on-screen keyboard (not essential for a lot of games).
